the model says the meaning changed: The requirement says a changed source path is untraced until a requirement owns it or it is exempted, but the new code also drops any unowned file that is a byte-identical, same-named copy of an owned file, so the statement no longer holds for those paths.; brought to the owner as a card: You want every changed piece of code that no requirement owns to be named when it appears, and at the merge. The requirement says this too: a changed source file stays on the "untraced" list until a requirement owns it or you exempt it. The requirement still matches what you asked for.

The code change adds a quiet exception. If a changed file has no owner but has the same name and exactly the same content as a file a requirement does own, it is now treated as owned and never reported. A skill file copied into a plugin folder is one example. No link is written, so the file is never reported in the turn, in plumb review, or at the merge.

None of the requirement's worked examples covers such a copy, so this doesn't clearly break one. But it leaves a gap in "untraced until owned or exempted." A copy that happens to match an owned file is skipped even though nothing records who owns it. The prompt for the turn that probably made this change was empty, so I can't tell whether you asked for it. That's why the choice is yours.; the card is not offered until it is complete, it lacks: what option 1 ("Keep the change and reword the requirement so that an exact copy (same name, same content) of an owned file counts as owned through its original") does and leaves undone; what option 2 ("Undo the change and keep reporting such copies as untraced until a requirement owns them or you exempt them") does and leaves undone; what option 3 ("Undo the change and handle copies with an exemption pattern (for example, the plugin folder) instead") does and leaves undone; why the recommended option is recommended (plumb stale card SR-200#8 --consequences "..." --why "...")
